Subject: production generation failures — seeing 503s and model timeouts

Priyom / Redwood team,

We started seeing large numbers of 503s and timeouts against your text-generation endpoint around 08:57 PDT. The impact is widespread (several dozen customer-facing requests failing) and correlates with longer tail latencies on tokens >512. Sample errors attached (error_sample_20270811.txt).

Immediate ask: can Redwood confirm whether there is an active degradation affecting our region (us-west) and whether there's an available fallback (re-route to dedicated pool / lower ortho model) we can flip to? We need an ETA for mitigation.

Severity: Production customer impact.
Environment: finly-prod (api keys scoped to FIN-7891).

Thanks,
Catherine

Subject: Re: production generation failures — seeing 503s and model timeouts

Catherine — thank you for the quick heads-up and the sample file. We've stood up an incident bridge and are assembling the cross-functional response.

Short answers now:
- We see elevated tail latencies in us-west for generation requests and a small set of backend nodes exhibiting KV cache pressure.
- We've opened a bridge (Zoom link + dial-in in bridge-join.ics) and asked infra to push a safe failover policy to re-route your traffic to a compatible model variant in the dedicated pool to reduce latency while we remediate.

Bridge details (joining now):
- Bridge host: priyom.das@redwood.com
- Start: 09:20 PDT
- Temporary mitigation: re-route to rfl-1-small model variant (throughput-optimized) — immediate flip if you authorize.

Request: please reply with approval to flip traffic to smaller model (we anticipate minor quality delta, will track metrics) and copy any internal Finly folks who must be on the bridge.

We'll keep updates on this thread and in the bridge notes doc.

—Priyom

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 11 Aug 2027 09:22:57 -0700
Subject: Re: production generation failures — seeing 503s and model timeouts

Joining bridge now. Quick tactical notes from infra: 
- Root cause signal: quick analysis of logs shows sustained memory growth in a subset of LLM workers serving larger context windows; KV cache eviction thrashing observed.
- Immediate mitigation plan: apply routing rule to divert 80% of Finly prod traffic to dedicated rfl-1-small instances (lower mem footprint), keep 20% on main pool for quality comparison. We'll also enable aggressive KV-cache eviction thresholds for affected nodes.
- Estimated time to complete switch: ~6 minutes after authorization.

If Finly approves, we'll execute and monitor latency, error-rate, and quality (sampled). If quality hit >3% regression on key prompts, auto-fallback back to main pool will be available.

Ben

Subject: Executive summary — Finly production impact and commitments

Catherine / David,

I wanted to step in with a concise executive summary for your leadership and customers while the engineering team completes mitigation. Key points for your stakeholders: 

- Impact: transient generation failures and elevated tail latency in Finly production beginning ~08:57 PDT; affecting some customer requests regionally in us-west.
- Mitigation underway: Redwood is routing 80% of traffic to a throughput-optimized variant to reduce tail latency; infra is applying eviction thresholds and collecting diagnostic dumps.
- Customer experience: brief quality delta possible for a small subset of requests; major functionality preserved.
- Commitments: 
  * Immediate: reduce customer-facing errors — target <0.5% error rate within 10 minutes of route flip.
  * Near term: full remediation plan and postmortem within 72 hours (action owners assigned).
  * Compensation: if a production SLA threshold is breached we will work with Finly on a proportional credit; account team will follow up.

I'll host a short post-incident review with your PMs once we have the diagnostic artifacts; please let me know availability for a 45-minute sync tomorrow.

Thanks for your patience — we'll continue to provide live updates.

Best,

Team — thank you for the rapid response and for the transparency. The reroute to the smaller instance reduced errors to normal levels within ~8 minutes and our customers are reporting stabilized behavior. We've accepted Marissa's invite for the postmortem and request the following be covered:

- Timeline of events and root cause analysis (heap/kv dump findings)
- Why eviction thrashing started for this context distribution and what guards will prevent recurrence
- Any requested config changes on Finly's side (prompt truncation guidance, max-seq default)
- Proposed SLA/credit calculation if thresholds were crossed

We appreciate Redwood's quick mitigation. Please include the bridge notes link and share the postmortem draft when available.

Catherine
